title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
statement: In an n by n grid, 0 is clear and 1 is blocked. Walk from the top-left corner to the bottom-right, moving to any of the EIGHT surrounding cells. Return the number of CELLS on the shortest clear path, counting both ends, or -1 if there is none.
constraints: the answer counts cells visited, not steps taken, so a 1x1 clear grid answers 1
hints: Every move costs the same, so breadth-first search finds the shortest path; no priority queue is needed.
The only differences from a normal grid search are eight offsets instead of four, and that the answer counts cells rather than edges.

Check both endpoints before you start: if the start or the goal is blocked the answer is -1 immediately. Mark cells visited as you enqueue them, or the eight-way branching will queue the same cell many times over.
